findings.evidence: Positivity.lean:134 `def g1 (ρ : SpinDensity)`, :139 `def h1 (ρ : SpinDensity) : ℝ := ρ.mat idxPP idxMM`; ComplexSpinDensity.lean:128 `def deltaQ : ℝ := PDF.g1 ρ.re`, :133 `def transversity : ℂ := ρ.mat idxPP idxMM`. Rubric: consistency with adjacent declarations beats a theoretically better name.
findings.fix: Pick one vocabulary across the pair: either name the complex ones `g1`/`h1` to match `PDF.g1`/`PDF.h1`, or, if `deltaQ`/`transversity` are the better physics names, rename the real `g1`/`h1` to match in this PR (the no-compatibility policy permits the in-repo rename).
findings.issue: `SpinDensityC.deltaQ` is by definition `PDF.g1 ρ.re` (line 128) and `SpinDensityC.transversity` is the analogue of `PDF.h1`, so the same two quantities carry two names inside one namespace. The lemma names then mix vocabularies: `g1_re : PDF.g1 ρ.re = ρ.deltaQ` (168), `h1_re` (173), `SpinDensity.deltaQ_toSpinDensityC : ρ.toSpinDensityC.deltaQ = PDF.g1 ρ` (355), `f1_add_deltaQ` vs `PDF.f1_add_g1`, `abs_deltaQ_le_f1` vs `PDF.abs_g1_le_f1`, `two_mul_norm_transversity_le_diag` vs `PDF.two_mul_abs_h1_le_diag`. A reader grepping `g1`/`h1` does not find the complex API and vice versa.

findings.evidence: Positivity.lean:129 `def f1 (ρ : SpinDensity)` is in `namespace PDF`, not `SpinDensity`; ComplexSpinDensity.lean:124 `def f1 : ℝ := PDF.f1 ρ.re` inside `namespace SpinDensityC` — the explicit `PDF.` qualifier is required precisely because the inner `f1` shadows.
findings.fix: Make the two sides agree: move the real `f1`/`g1`/`h1` into the `SpinDensity` namespace (so `ρ.f1` works for both and the `PDF.` prefixes disappear), or define the complex ones as `PDF.f1C`-style siblings in `PDF` rather than inside `SpinDensityC`.
findings.issue: The real observables live in `PDF` (`PDF.f1 (ρ : SpinDensity)`), the complex ones in `PDF.SpinDensityC` (`ρ.f1`). So `f1` names two declarations in overlapping scope, dot notation works on one type only, and the file has to write `PDF.f1 ρ.re` / `PDF.g1 ρ.re` everywhere to disambiguate (lines 124, 128, 164, 168, 173, 178, 260, 266).

findings.evidence: Line 123 `lemma re_star_dotProduct_mulVec_ofReal [Fintype n] (M : Matrix n n 𝕜) (x : n → ℝ)` vs line 142 `lemma re_star_dotProduct_map_ofReal_mulVec [Fintype n] (M : Matrix n n ℝ) (x : n → 𝕜)`.
findings.fix: Make the coerced object explicit in the first name, e.g. `re_star_ofReal_dotProduct_mulVec_ofReal`, so the vector coercion is visible where it occurs.
findings.issue: `re_star_dotProduct_mulVec_ofReal` (vector is coerced, matrix is over 𝕜) and `re_star_dotProduct_map_ofReal_mulVec` (matrix is coerced, vector is over 𝕜) differ only in the position of `ofReal`; the trailing `mulVec_ofReal` in the first reads most naturally as a coerced matrix, which is exactly the other lemma.

summary: The complex structure renames two of the three leading-twist quantities (`g1` → `deltaQ`, `h1` → `transversity`) relative to its real sibling in the same namespace, and puts them in a different namespace than the real ones (`SpinDensityC.f1` vs `PDF.f1`), producing mixed-vocabulary lemma names and a shadowed `f1`. One confusable lemma pair in PosSemidef.lean.
